PullRequest.Title: mcp: show where built-in MCP servers come from

Fixes #338719

The MCP server details in Chat Customizations didn't say where built-in servers come from. The header showed a made-up `mcp.json`, and Configuration only said "No definition is available". This PR uses what the agent runtime already reports about each server (its source, display name and contributing plugin) to show the real origin, and explains when there's nothing to show.

### What you'll see

| MCP server | Before | Now |
|---|---|---|
| `github-mcp-server` (built into Copilot CLI) | Made-up `mcp.json` label; "No definition is available" | **Built-in: Copilot**. Configuration explains that Copilot sets it up, with an **Open Settings** link to `chat.agentHost.githubMcpServer.enabled` |
| Copilot connector (managed by Copilot) | Opaque name (`github-copilot-connector-…`), made-up `mcp.json` | The connector's real name (e.g. "Linear"), **Managed by Copilot**, and an explanation |
| GitHub server from the Copilot Chat extension (local chat) | No source | **Built-in: GitHub Copilot Chat**, linking to the extension; the `...` menu gains **Show Extension** |
| Added via **MCP: Add Server → Add to Current Agent Session** | Could land under Built-In; no definition | Listed under **User**, labelled **Agent host configuration**, with its definition |
| Reported as user or workspace config, but no file is known | Made-up `mcp.json` label | **User configuration** / **Workspace configuration** |
| Configured in an `mcp.json` or another app's config file | File link and Edit Configuration | Unchanged. Built-in rows backed by another app's file (e.g. Claude Desktop) also get **Show Configuration** in the `...` menu |

### How it works

- The Copilot agent host forwards the runtime's `displayName` and `sourcePlugin` (from `session.mcp.list`) as optional, namespaced `_meta` on MCP server customizations. Other agent hosts can leave them out.
- The details page shows where a server comes from when there's no file to open, and an explanation when the agent owns the definition.
- `getMcpServers()` also exposes the definition the agent host's own configuration holds for a server, so servers added there show their definition.

### Notes for reviewers

- Display names replace the row label only for managed servers. For other servers the runtime falls back to the server's own advertised title, which would rename servers that users configured.
- Copilot Chat's own servers keep their extension ID (to link to it) but stay under Built-In.
- `GITHUB_MCP_SERVER_NAME` moved to `platform/agentHost/common/githubEndpoints.ts` so UI code can use it; the node module re-exports it.
- Not in this PR: showing a built-in server's tools or instructions, or its actual definition (the Copilot SDK doesn't expose it).

### How to test

1. In a Copilot CLI agent session, open Chat Customizations → MCP Servers and select `github-mcp-server`. The header says "Built-in: Copilot", Configuration explains why there's no definition, and **Open Settings** opens `chat.agentHost.githubMcpServer.enabled`.
2. Run **MCP: Add Server → Add to Current Agent Session**. The server is listed under User with "Agent host configuration" and its definition.
3. In a local chat, select Copilot's GitHub server. The header links to GitHub Copilot Chat, and `...` → **Show Extension** opens it.
4. A server from `.vscode/mcp.json` still shows its file link and Edit Configuration.

The `EmbeddedMcpDetailBuiltinAgent` and `EmbeddedMcpDetailBuiltinExtension` component fixtures show the new details states.

Scenarios.Scenario: Agent-host MCP inventory discovery and publication for Copilot and Codex sessions
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Copilot performs the existing mcp.list RPC, maps the returned servers, and applies the inventory before publishing changed customizations; Codex applies its already-materialized inventory when sessions or configuration change. The diff adds display-name/source-plugin metadata and an in-memory provenance lookup but no new required boundary.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One RPC for initial seeding and each existing inventory invalidation, with an existing retry only if a lifecycle event overtakes the snapshot; one result covers all servers.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same mcp.list RPC and optional user-server-name lookup already occurred; the diff only forwards two additional optional fields from each returned server.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The RPC must finish before the refreshed inventory is applied, exactly as before the diff.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Session customization update dispatch carrying MCP server state and metadata
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one existing update per server whose published customization changes; unchanged inventories remain deduplicated by structural equality.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Per-server customization updates already crossed this boundary for state/source changes; display/source-plugin changes can now legitimately trigger the same update so the UI can reflect them.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Updates notify clients after in-memory inventory reconciliation; payloads gain at most two short optional metadata strings per changed server.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of MCP servers in one inventory and, for Codex, number of live sessions sharing the inventory. Typical inventories are small; application remains serial and transaction-coalesced per controller.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Copilot inventory refreshes are versioned so stale concurrent requests are discarded; controller application is synchronous and serial inside one transaction. Codex iterates sessions serially. No new burst or parallel boundary was introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The controller retains the latest per-server customization and preserves metadata across lifecycle-only updates. Unchanged inventories compare equal and emit nothing. No new cache, miss retry, or negative-cache behavior was added.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the RPC, transaction, equality deduplication, and new metadata helper call paths were traced directly.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Very large inventories would add another linear published-customization scan/allocation during first/restored top-level reconciliation, but it is in-memory, short-lived, and not repeated on normal lifecycle updates because the live customization is retained.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. Added CPU/allocation and serialized bytes are bounded by server count and required to publish the new metadata; no new external call, concurrency burst, or hot repeated work was introduced.

Scenarios.Scenario: Opening, refreshing, and searching the Chat Customizations MCP server list
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The widget reads an already-materialized server snapshot, matches local/runtime/host entries, computes grouping and membership, then renders or updates visible rows. Search remains delayed/coalesced before filtering.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Installed, built-in, connector, and active-session MCP server counts; effective cardinality is one deduplicated row per presented server after matching.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Filtering and rendering are synchronous on the UI thread; search uses the pre-existing delayed filter, and customization events run one serial refresh/update pass. No new asynchronous fan-out was introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The widget consumes existing observable/service snapshots. Membership signatures now include the display label so a real label change rebuilds rows; state-only updates continue using row updates. No cold/warm external cache behavior changed.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: list event handlers, matching, membership comparison, row listeners, and search debounce were inspected.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: A display-name-only inventory change can cause a full list rebuild, but such changes are inventory events rather than keystroke/frame events and realistic lists are bounded; the work is necessary to update the visible label.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. New work is short string validation/comparison and one additional label search predicate; there are no new filesystem, network, IPC, layout-read, or process boundaries on list refresh.

Scenarios.Scenario: Selecting an MCP server detail and invoking provenance, settings, or configuration actions
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Selection constructs one detail input and renders provenance plus either the existing source-backed definition, one host-held configuration, or an unavailable-definition message. Extension/settings/configuration actions execute only after explicit user clicks.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read a source configuration file to display or edit its MCP definition
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one read for the selected source-backed server render, plus an edit-time read only when no range is known.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Source-backed details already read the selected configuration file. The new host-configuration path serializes already-held state instead of adding a read.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The display read remains on the selected detail's loading path; host-only provenance/configuration states added by the diff do not perform this read.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Open Settings, extension details, or show configuration through existing command/service APIs
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One command/service call per explicit user click.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: These provenance-specific actions were unavailable, so there was no corresponding call; the diff does not invoke them eagerly.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Off the initial render critical path; only the selected user action waits for it.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One selected server and the size of its single configuration object or source file; there is no per-list-item eager detail work.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One selected detail generation is active; generation checks discard stale file-read results. Click actions execute individually with no burst scheduling.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The code editor/model remains lazily created on the first actual definition. Host-held configuration is already in session state; no new cache or repeated fetch is used.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: selection construction, render branches, lazy editor creation, filesystem reads, and click handlers were traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: A user-provided host configuration can be large and is JSON-serialized when selected, but only one selected definition is processed and this is the requested visible content.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. New provenance DOM is small and on demand; newly reachable IPC actions are user-triggered and off render, while existing source-file I/O is unchanged.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance review across all 19 changed files. The change forwards bounded MCP provenance metadata, exposes an already-materialized host configuration, and adds on-demand provenance UI. No high-confidence, actionable performance regression was found; no findings were submitted.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
